The '''2020–21 La Liga''' season, also known as '''La Liga Santander''' due to sponsorship reasons, was the 90th since its establishment. The season began on 12 September 2020 and concluded on 23 May 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/52848048|title=La Liga to resume on 11 June; 2020-21 season to start in September|date=29 May 2020|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> The fixtures were announced on 31 August 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/noticias/sorteo-del-calendario-primera-division-manana-lunes-1830-sede-rfef|title=El sorteo del calendario de Primera División, mañana lunes a las 18:30 en la sede de la RFEF|language=es|date=30 August 2020|website=rfef.es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/el-calendario-oficial-de-laliga-santander-2020-21-a-un-clic|title=El calendario oficial de LaLiga Santander 2020/21, a un clic|language=es|date=31 August 2020|website=laliga.com|access-date=17 April 2021|archive-date=14 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200914052744/https://www.laliga.com/noticias/el-calendario-oficial-de-laliga-santander-2020-21-a-un-clic/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] were the defending champions, after winning a record 34th title in the previous season. [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] and [[Elche CF|Elche]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2019–20 Segunda División]]. They replaced [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] and [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], who were relegated to the [[2020–21 Segunda División]].

Exceptionally, this season the five [[Substitute (association football)|substitutions]] were maintained in a maximum of three rounds per team, adopted in May 2020 due to the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports#Association football|impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-espana.net/2020/09/08/la-liga-to-continue-with-five-substitutions-for-teams-this-season|title=La Liga to continue with five substitutions for teams this season|first=Colin|last=Millar|date=8 September 2020}}</ref>

[[Atlético Madrid]] won their eleventh La Liga title on the last day of the season, after a 2–1 comeback win against [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]], who were relegated with the defeat. It was their first title since [[2013–14 La Liga|2013–14]]. [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and Real Madrid were the only other teams to have won the title since Atlético Madrid last did so.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/22/real-valladolid-atletico-madrid-la-liga-match-report|title=Atlético Madrid clinch La Liga title after Luis Suárez seals win at Real Valladolid|date=22 May 2021|access-date=22 May 2021|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of twenty teams contested the league, including seventeen sides from the [[2019–20 La Liga|2019–20 season]] and three promoted from the [[2019–20 Segunda División]]. This included the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2020 Segunda División play-offs|promotion play-offs]].

;Teams relegated to Segunda División

The first team to be relegated from [[La Liga]] were [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], after a 0–1 loss to [[Derbi barceloní|city rivals]] [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on 8 July 2020, ending their 26-year stay in the top tier.<ref>{{cite news |title=European roundup: Suárez's winner for Barça condemns Espanyol to relegation|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jul/08/luis-suarezs-winner-for-barcelona-condemns-espanyol-to-relegation#:~:text=Espanyol%2C%20one%20of%20Spain's%20most,24%20points%20after%2035%20games.|work=The Guardian| date=8 July 2020 |access-date=17 July 2020}}</ref> The second team to be relegated were [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], following a 1–2 home defeat against [[Granada CF|Granada]] on 16 July 2020, suffering an immediate return to the second division.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mallorca Set For Relegation With Loss To Granada|url=https://www.beinsports.com/us/laliga/video/mallorca-set-for-relegation-with-loss-to-gran/1505337|publisher=beIN Sports USA|access-date=17 July 2020}}</ref> The third and final team to be relegated were [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], after drawing 2–2 against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 19 July 2020 in their final game of the season. This ended ''Lega'''s four-year stint in the first tier.<ref>{{cite web|title=Leganés relegated after holding champions Real Madrid|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/07/19/football/1595181480_644867.html|publisher=AS|access-date=19 July 2020|archive-date=19 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719191511/https://en.as.com/en/2020/07/19/football/1595181480_644867.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;Teams promoted from Segunda División

On 12 July 2020, [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] became the first side to mathematically be promoted, assured of a return to the top flight after a fourteen-year absence following [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]]'s 4–2 win against [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cadiz return to LaLiga Santander|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/cadiz-return-to-laliga-santander|publisher=La Liga|date=12 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|archive-date=11 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230811091132/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/cadiz-return-to-laliga-santander|url-status=dead}}</ref> The second team to earn promotion were [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], following their 3–0 win against [[CD Numancia|Numancia]] on 17 July 2020. This marked an immediate return to the first division after a season away.<ref>{{cite web |title=Huesca returns to the First Division a year later|date=18 July 2020 |url=https://sportsfinding.com/huesca-returns-to-the-first-division-a-year-later/50803/|publisher=Sportsfinding|access-date=18 July 2020}}</ref> The final team to achieve promotion were [[Elche CF|Elche]] on 23 August 2020, following a 1–0 aggregate victory over [[Girona FC|Girona]] in the final of the promotion play-offs, sealing a return to La Liga after a five-year absence.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elche Secure Promotion To LaLiga With 1-0 Win Over Girona|url=https://www.beinsports.com/us/laliga-smartbank/video/elche-secure-promotion-to-laliga-with-1-0-win/1529742|publisher=beIN Sports USA|access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy|Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest goals-to-games ratio. A goalkeeper had to have played at least 28 games of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/primera-division/zamora.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander - MARCA.com|work=MARCA.com|date=4 September 2017}}</ref>
